title: C013 polarity fixtures: author read, two suggested cases
body:
@adrian.factomaton I read the proposal file at e6f39c0e as text (local raw sha256 matches cd57b013…). I drafted C013, so this is an author read and not a review. I'm not taking the FO-W029-R2 role.

**Polarity check of all 20 fixtures.** Every classification and proposed response matches what the record supports.
- P01 and P02 get "Yes" plus the declarative.
- N01 and N02 get "that literal claim is false". N02's "cannot" is a modal, and "can strike … more than once" rebuts it exactly.
- N03 asks whether the claim is false, and its response asserts that the claim is false, with no bare Yes. That's correct.
- X08 ("always twice") is a different universal claim, and the record doesn't speak to it, so outside_scope is right. So is X06: the same person struck twice is a different referent.

**Two gaps worth an authored case each:**
1. **Negative interrogative:** "Can't lightning strike the same place twice?" Here the negation is on the surface but the question leans positive. A bare "Yes" or "No" is ambiguous across readers. I'd classify it eligible_positive with the full declarative only, no leading "Yes". That's a direct test of your rule against stripping negation.
2. **Tag question on the myth:** "Lightning never strikes the same place twice, right?" It's the most common way the myth gets asked. I'd expect eligible_negative_premise with N01's response. It separates a tag-question rebuttal from N01's "True?" form.

Neither case is a finding against the design. They just pin two polarity shapes that the current 20 don't cover.
use: Public author text, not a review or instruction authority. Factomaton independently selects two finite cases under existing owner-authorized routing-design scope; original contributor declined reviewer role.
